title: Ushuaia: the city at the end of the world
meta_description: Ushuaia guide: Beagle Channel, Tierra del Fuego National Park, penguins, hiking, how to get there and where to stay.
hero_subtitle: Between the mountains and the Beagle Channel, at Argentina's southern tip.
photo_alt: Penguins on the Beagle Channel shore

why_visit.title: The Beagle Channel
why_visit.text: Boat trips among islands with sea lions, birds and the Les Eclaireurs lighthouse.

why_visit.title: Penguins
why_visit.text: In season you can visit the Martillo Island penguin colony, with trips from the city.

why_visit.title: Tierra del Fuego National Park
why_visit.text: Forests, lakes and bays a few kilometers away, with trails for every level.

activities.title: Beagle Channel boat trip
activities.text: Ushuaia's classic outing: islands with marine wildlife and views of the city from the water.

activities.title: Tierra del Fuego National Park
activities.text: Coastal and forest trails, lakes and Lapataia Bay. Go on your own or on a tour.

activities.title: End of the World Train
activities.text: A historic ride that enters the national park. Great with kids.

activities.title: Laguna Esmeralda
activities.text: A half-day hike through forest and peat bog to a lake of intense green.

activities.title: Martial Glacier
activities.text: A trail climbing from the edge of the city, with views of the channel.

activities.title: Maritime and Prison Museum
activities.text: Housed in Ushuaia's old prison, it tells the story of the city and southern navigation.

how_to_get_there:
By plane: Malvinas Argentinas International Airport (USH) has direct flights from Buenos Aires, about three and a half hours, and from other cities.

Overland: from the mainland you cross the Strait of Magellan by ferry and pass through Chilean territory. It's a long trip that requires valid documents.

Around town: taxis, private cars and tours with transfers. The national park is a few kilometers away.

where_to_stay.budget: Hostels with shared rooms and guest kitchens, plus campsites in season. They're the most affordable option and a good place to meet other travelers.
where_to_stay.midrange: Inns, cabins and small hotels, often with breakfast included. Cabins with kitchens suit families and groups.
where_to_stay.luxury: Upscale hotels and lodges with landscape views, spas or tours included. Book them well in advance.

practical_tips.title: Best time
practical_tips.text: In summer the days are very long and there are more tours. In winter, Ushuaia is a snow destination.

practical_tips.title: Changeable weather
practical_tips.text: Wind and sudden weather changes are part of the trip. Dress in layers and always carry a windbreaker.

practical_tips.title: Book ahead
practical_tips.text: In high season, lodging and tours fill up. It's best to book as soon as you have your dates.

practical_tips.title: Prices and payments
practical_tips.text: Prices change often: check current rates before you travel and carry some cash as well as cards.

closing: Ushuaia combines sea, mountains and forest within a few kilometers. Three or four days cover the essentials.
